headline: Packaged pipelines and locus-set design make pathogen typing calls reproducible
label: Pathogen Genomics Method Evaluation
summary: Sequence-to-call workflows are now packaged for reproducibility, and cumulative cgMLST tests finer locus sets for nested Klebsiella groups.
synthesis: The dominant thread is converting raw sequence output into defined, reproducible calls through packaged, containerized workflows. BIP processes FASTQ output into COI barcodes, separating target from non-target sequences and assigning BINs. MAP provides a Docker-installable metabarcoding workflow for highly multiplexed, replicated designs, and neissflow packages Neisseria gonorrhoeae genomic epidemiology in Nextflow. A separate evaluative strand, represented here by cumulative cgMLST, addresses discrimination: nested core-loci sets raise pairwise allelic distances 5.6-fold over the KpSC scheme in Klebsiella pneumoniae. What is new relative to standard typing is locus-set design for resolving nested phylogenetic groups, alongside pipelines that bundle barcode, metabarcoding and typing steps into single installable tools.
